system_overview: A foundational module that defines reachability in a directed graph. It provides the mathematical framework for expressing which nodes can be reached from a given set of starting nodes by following directed edges. This module serves as a library imported by the algorithm specifications and proof modules in the reachability suite.
actors_and_components: No active actors. The module defines a directed graph represented by a set of nodes and a successor function that maps each node to the set of nodes reachable by a single edge. It provides operators for paths and reachability.
state_variables: No state variables. This is a constant-level module defining operators over the graph structure.
additional_assumptions: The successor function is assumed to map each node to a subset of the node set. The graph is represented using the successor-function style rather than an edge-set style, though the two representations are mathematically equivalent. Paths are defined as sequences where each consecutive pair of nodes is connected by an edge. Reachability from a set of nodes is defined as the set of all nodes reachable via some path from any node in the starting set.
